title: SLO Thermostat: adaptive trigger & autotune for canary evictions
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: Canary rollouts currently use fixed hard thresholds for latency and error rates which cause noisy aborts during traffic variance and sometimes fail to protect against cost regressions (token cost spikes) or throughput drops. Goal: Build an "SLO Thermostat" service that ingests per-canary telemetry (latency P50/P95/P99, 4xx/5xx error rates, tokens-per-request, throughput) and produces adaptive eviction decisions and tuned trigger thresholds. The Thermostat should support composite signals, cohort baselining, and a tunable confidence window to avoid flapping. It must be pluggable into the rollout controller and expose audit logs and a simulation mode for operators.
acceptance_criteria: Thermostat exposes an API for canary evaluation that returns one of: keep, throttle, evict, or hold_with_monitoring
Adaptive thresholds are computed by combining baseline cohort metrics and a configurable sensitivity factor; documented algorithm and tests exist
SLO signals supported: latency (P50/P95/P99), error_rate (4xx/5xx), tokens_per_request, throughput; signal fusion described in spec
Simulation mode can replay a historical traffic window against a new model and output the eviction decision timeline
Integration test validates no more than 2% false-positive evictions on production-like traffic (based on historical replay)
Audit trail recorded to Console tracing for every decision with the contributing signals and tuned threshold values
tasks: Write design doc and algorithm sketch (Bayesian baseline + hysteresis + cost-normalization)
Prototype Thermostat service (Go) with lightweight in-memory windowing
Implement signal adapters for runtime telemetry (Prometheus exporter + pull API)
Integrate Thermostat decision API into rollout controller canary evaluator
Add simulation/replay harness and two production replay jobs for top-3 customers
End-to-end tests and chaos tests for traffic variance and partial infra outages
Dashboard widgets for tuned thresholds and decision heatmap in Console
decisions: Prefer a Bayesian change-detection core with configurable priors rather than pure fixed thresholds to reduce sensitivity to low-volume cohorts
Include tokens_per_request as a first-class signal to capture cost regressions for generative models
Implement a 3-state hysteresis (green/yellow/red) with configurable hold windows to avoid flaps
Run simulation mode in the control plane only; eviction RPCs must be audited and rate-limited
tradeoffs: Complex adaptive logic increases operational surface area and requires more observability; mitigated by shipping simulation first
Bayesian priors reduce false positives for low-volume canaries but can delay detection for abrupt regressions; provide emergency hard-stop thresholds for critical customers
Per-cohort baselining improves accuracy but requires grouping heuristics and storage for cohort baselines
telemetry: Per-model per-canary 4xx and 5xx counts and rates
Tokens per request and tokens per-minute for canary cohort
Throughput (requests/s) and CPU/GPU utilization for serving units
test_plan: Unit tests for Bayesian thresholds and hysteresis logic
Replay historical traffic for the last 90 days for three sample models and verify decisions vs. known incidents
Chaos: synthetic latency spikes combined with traffic surges to ensure no more than one unintended eviction per 1000 canaries
Load test Thermostat API at 10k evaluations/s and measure 99th percentile decision latency < 50ms
Security review of audit logs (ensure no PII persisted)
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Simulation mode with dashboards for two weeks; compare Thermostat recommendations against current fixed-thresholds
Stage 2: Opt-in canary evaluator for internal teams (traffic limited to 0.5% per model) with manual approve for evictions
Stage 3: Auto-evict for non-critical customers behind an emergency hard-stop threshold; monitor false-positive rate
Stage 4: Gradual ramp to broad auto-evict after 6 weeks if false-positive rate < 2% and operator feedback is green
